title: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing'

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing'
evidence_packet.lead: A drone unit at Greater Manchester Police is regularly following and helping to catch criminals
evidence_packet.summary: A drone unit at Greater Manchester Police is regularly following and helping to catch criminals
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing' - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Police have been using drones to track down bike thieves across the north of Manchester By Richard Stead North West Published 50 minutes ago Drones have been described a "the future of policing" after they were used to help seize 130 illegal off-road bikes across north Manchester in the less than a year. The fleet of drones is being used by Greater Manchester Police instead of the force helicopter because drones are cheaper to use and more discreet. Insp Dan Pickavance, from GMP's North Manchester Neighbourhood Policing Team, said: "All police forces can use drones - particularly in urban areas - and it means we can safely take illegal off-road bikes off the streets. "Using drones is without doubt the future of neighbourhood policing and this is an essential game-changer for us going forward." Image caption, Dan Pickavance, a neighbourhood police inspector for North Manchester, was able to monitor the images from the drone The BBC followed a police operation in which a drone was used to recover a stolen bike that had been spotted in Boggart Hole Clough. The drone was used to follow the bike to an address in nearby Charlestown, where police officers on the ground searched the property and arrested three suspects. The operation was directed by a senior police officer in the back of a van, using live images from the drone which were relayed onto a screen. title: Kimpton Clocktower workers to strike during Manchester Pride

evidence_packet.title: Kimpton Clocktower workers to strike during Manchester Pride
evidence_packet.lead: The action will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union
evidence_packet.summary: The action will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Staff at a Manchester hotel will be on strike during the city's upcoming Pride weekend Unite union members working at the Kimpton Clocktower hotel and its bar, The Refuge, will striking over working conditions on Saturday - the second day of Manchester Pride The strike will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union. It comes after the hotel advertised Pride weekend package stays and a free two-day Pride celebration to take place at the hotel's Refuge bar A spokesperson for InterContinental Hotels Group UK (IHG), which owns the Kimpton Clocktower, said it has plans to minimise disruption - adding "the hotel and The Refuge continue to operate as normal" "We are aware of concerns raised by a small number of colleagues at The Refuge at the Kimpton Clocktower Manchester, who have decided to take industrial action," the IHG spokesperson said "We have taken those concerns seriously and continue to engage with colleagues through well established, direct feedback channels."

title: Man denies Piccadilly Gardens rape of girl, 17

evidence_packet.title: Man denies Piccadilly Gardens rape of girl, 17
evidence_packet.lead: Abdul Shinwari, 24, pleads not guilty to charges of rape, strangulation and drug offences
evidence_packet.summary: Abdul Shinwari, 24, pleads not guilty to charges of rape, strangulation and drug offences
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Man denies Piccadilly Gardens rape of girl, 17 - BBC News Image source, Google Maps Image caption, Abdul Shinwari, 24, pleaded not guilty to raping a "vulnerable" 17-year-old girl on 14 July Published 25 August 2026 A man has denied raping a teenage girl in Manchester. Abdul Shinwari, 24, also pleaded not guilty to strangling the "vulnerable" 17-year-old and denied drugs offences. Shinwari appeared at Manchester Crown Court via video link from HMP Forest Bank, Salford, earlier to deny one count of rape, one of intentional strangulation, one of supplying cannabis and one of being concerned in the supply of crack cocaine. The rape offence is alleged to have been committed at about 01:30 BST on 14 July, on Hope Street near Piccadilly Gardens. He will be held in custody until a further hearing on 21 December, ahead of a trial on 18 January 2027. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Almost £1bn government cash to North West for 7,500 new homes - BBC News Image source, EPA/Shutterstock By Hannah Richardson Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 25 August 2026 The government is to give nearly £1bn to the North West to deliver about 7,500 new homes as part of plans to "build the country out of a housing crisis". A share of up to £10bn has been announced for councils and housing associations nationally in the first wave of government funding to boost "genuinely affordable homes". Greater Manchester has been given the largest share of the six mayoral areas to benefit from this round, with Liverpool City Region set to deliver 3,100 homes supported by £380m. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged the largest post-war council housebuilding programme to tackle severe shortages and homelessness, saying "no child should be raised in a hostel room". Nationally, almost 180,000 children are growing up without a permanent home, according to the government. The Prime Minister said the cash will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers, and will be spent on building "genuinely affordable homes". Around 60% of the more than 70,000 properties are expected to be social rent. They will be in the first wave of Labour's £39bn 10-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme , external . The government said it aimed to help families "trapped in temporary accommodation or stuck on housing waiting lists' into safe, secure homes". Image caption, Liverpool City Region is set to deliver 3,100 homes Burnham said: "No child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait ten years for a front door of their own. title: Debt-ridden Warrington Borough Council announces £51.2m more cuts

evidence_packet.title: Debt-ridden Warrington Borough Council announces £51.2m more cuts
evidence_packet.lead: The additional savings plan brings the total cuts to about £90m
evidence_packet.summary: The additional savings plan brings the total cuts to about £90m
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cash-strapped Warrington Borough Council is planning more than £50m of extra cuts It is set to publish a report detailing a further £51.2m of savings which, alongside £39m of cuts previously identified by the authority in March, brings the total to about £90m This included ending funding for walking day, selling off assets, cutting street lighting and stopping free parking in the town centre The Labour administration said the cuts were aimed at "ensuring the council's future sustainability", but the Liberal Democrats said there was "little confidence" in the administration The new savings proposals will be discussed at the council's scrutiny committee on 7 September, before being considered for approval by cabinet and endorsement by full council The council's cabinet member for finance, councillor Denis Matthews, said the council faced a £179m funding gap up to 2030

title: Oldham community garden's food supply hit by dry summer

evidence_packet.title: Oldham community garden's food supply hit by dry summer
evidence_packet.lead: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
evidence_packet.summary: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from NorthernLily CIC, a social enterprise in Oldham , said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot summer, and the failed crops had to be composted "Normally we grow over a tonne of food, which equates to 12,700 meals worth, and we give that away to our community," said Victoria Holden "Unfortunately, I'm not sure we'll get to a tonne this year - and that's real fresh food that normally supports our community which is now not going to be available." "We lost a lot of plants. We had to just reduce everything down in the polytunnel to what could cope with that, sometimes, 55 degree heat," she said Holden said tropical plants like the chillies, gourds, aubergines and tomatoes had survived, but the produce was "about a quarter full to where it would normally be at this stage in the year"

title: 'Letters to Loved Ones' post box scheme launched in Cheshire East

evidence_packet.title: 'Letters to Loved Ones' post box scheme launched in Cheshire East
evidence_packet.lead: Letters will be handled confidentially and will not be opened or read, Cheshire East Council says
evidence_packet.summary: Letters will be handled confidentially and will not be opened or read, Cheshire East Council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: White post boxes have been introduced at cemeteries across Cheshire to give people a way to stay connected with loved ones who have died The Letters to Loved Ones scheme collects letters and returns the messages to the cemetery grounds through composting They would neither be opened nor read and would be handled with complete confidentiality, said Cheshire East Council "Grief is a deeply personal experience and we recognise that many people find comfort in continuing their connection with those they have lost," said councillor David Jefferay He said the authority had received a positive response to the initiative and he hoped it would bring comfort to those who used it "[It] provides a simple but meaningful outlet for remembrance, reflection and expression," he added

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Staff at a Manchester hotel will be on strike during the city's upcoming Pride weekend Unite union members working at the Kimpton Clocktower hotel and its bar, The Refuge, will striking over working conditions on Saturday - the second day of Manchester Pride The strike will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cash-strapped Warrington Borough Council is planning more than £50m of extra cuts It is set to publish a report detailing a further £51.2m of savings which, alongside £39m of cuts previously identified by the authority in March, brings the total to about £90m This included ending funding for walking day, selling off assets, cutting street lighting and stopping free parking in the town centre The Labour administration said the cuts were aimed at "ensuring the council's future sustainability", but the Liberal Democrats said there was "little confidence" in the administration The new savings proposals will be discussed at the council's scrutiny committee on 7 September, before being considered for approval by cabinet and endorsement by full council The council's cabinet member for finance, councillor Denis Matthews, said the council faced a £179m funding gap up to 2030

evidence_packet.summary: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from NorthernLily CIC, a social enterprise in Oldham , said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not surviv
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from NorthernLily CIC, a social enterprise in Oldham , said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot summer, and the failed crops had to be composted "Normally we grow over a tonne of food, which equates to 12,700 meals worth, and we give that away to our community," said Victoria Holden "Unfortunately, I'm not sure we'll get to a tonne this year - and that's real fresh food that normally supports our community which is now not going to be available." "We lost a lot of plants. We had to just reduce everything down in the polytunnel to what could cope with that, sometimes, 55 degree heat," she said Holden said tropical plants like the chillies, gourds, aubergines and tomatoes had survived, but the produce was "about a quarter full to where it would normally be at this stage in the year"

More tourists has meant ‘local people tend to avoid it’ Before the fire, people said litter would pile up with ‘rubbish everywhere’, empty beer bottles would be left behind, and barbecues lit despite a ban. So many cars turn up, Sarah White said: “They were blocking the roads. You couldn’t even get through at the time.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester could soon become a 20mph city - but not everyone is convinced Hundreds more streets are set for lower speed limits, but some have questioned whether it is the right approach. Supposedly a 30mph area, the road cuts right across the estate from east to west but many locals say there’s a major speeding problem It has got to the point where some people ‘struggle to cross the road’ at certain times of day because of how fast the cars go, and the amount of traffic congestion But everything could soon change under plans by Manchester council to slash speed limits to 20mph on hundreds of roads around Wythenshawe, including Hollyhedge The move was announced in August to bring Wythenshawe’s roads in line with other parts of the city, and reduce collisions Speed limits in many parts of Manchester have fallen in recent years under the same aim, with nearly 70 per cent of the network now at 20mph according to council figures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Radcliffe Radcliffe man, 22, ends up in court after chat with cyclist left them 'backing away in fear' Tyreece Bedford appeared at Manchester Crown Court Comments News Hope Gallagher 06:00, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Tyreece Bedford A man swiped a man's hat after pulling out what police believe was a knife. Tyreece Bedford, 22, found himself in the dock following the 'tomfoolery' last summer Manchester Crown Court heard a man he knew cycled past him on Pilkington Way, Radcliffe , on June 14, 2025. The cyclist turned back and approached Bedford The pair briefly spoke before Bedford took the man's hat. When he tried to get it back, Bedford brandished an object cops believe was a blade CCTV footage played in court showed the man backing away from Bedford. He was initially charged with threatening a person with a blade and theft, but instead pleaded guilty to the lesser charge of affray Prosecutor Brian Berlyne said: "The man backed away in apparent fear. He appears to believe it to be a weapon. Police believe it to have been a small knife."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Armed police called to Cheshire village after shots fired A 35-year-old man has been arrested at the scene News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 21:43, 25 Aug 2026 Updated 21:53, 25 Aug 2026 View Image Beauty Bank, Cheshire A man has been arrested after gunshots were heard in a Cheshire village. Armed police were called to reports of the incident in the Beauty Bank area of Whitegate near Northwich at around 5.45pm on Monday (August 24) A 35-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm in a public place. An air weapon was also found during a search of the area Detective Inspector Ross Hamilton, of Northwich CID, said: “Firearms offences are rare in Cheshire, and we treat all reports we receive extremely seriously “While on this occasion there were no reports of any injuries, the use of firearms in a public place can be extremely dangerous and there are also a number of legal consequences, including significant custodial sentences “Enquiries in relation to this incident remain ongoing and I would urge anyone with any information or footage which may aid our enquiries to call us on 101 or visit www.cheshire.police.uk/tell-us quoting IML 2402957.”

title: Stockport council announces big change to bin collections

evidence_packet.title: Stockport council announces big change to bin collections
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport w
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport w
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport will be affected by a major change to their bin collections later this year. The new system will be brought in before Christmas From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 The town hall’s Liberal Democrat administration said it has responded to complaints in recent weeks over how it collects bins across the borough. While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticis Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins. One resident called the situation ‘woke’, another said it was ‘petty’, and a councillor claimed some areas were being ‘pick More recently, the council was accused of flipflopping after a 'bizarre' incident was recorded on a doorbell camera, which the local authority later said was a mistake . Dave Bresnahan said: "It seems like they have gone from one extreme to another."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Sir Billy Boston: Wigan's greatest ever warrior A wad of cash spread out on a table in Cardiff led to an iconic rugby league career View 6 Images Sir Billy Boston News Paul Britton Reporter 16:29, 25 Aug 2026 A feared streak of pace combined with endless power and a ruthless desire to win Tough in the tackle - and even tougher to tackle as he graced the wings of rugby grounds across the world - Sir Billy Boston was arguably Wigan's greatest ever warrior. Yet outside of the sport his smile and personality were as endearing as his determination on the pitch was fier The rugby league legend, who has died aged 92 a month after the passing of his adored wife of 70 years, transcended generations He once scored more than 120 tries in one season alone and after being scouted by Wigan at the tender age of 19, he was the first non-white player to represent Great Britain during a Lions tour in 1954 - smashing a racial barrier in British sport His career as a globally-recognised, trailblazing black sports star inspired others to do what he was doing and work to achieve what he was achieving

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Trial of men accused of historic sexual offences against three girls in Rochdale due to start Tahir Rashid, Mohammed Saleem, Sucklane Shah, Amjad Mahmood, Iftaq Hussain and Arshad Mohammed deny all the charges they face News Andrew Bardsley Cou A jury in the trial of six men accused of historic sexual offences allegedly committed against three girls in Rochdale has been sworn in Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. He told jurors that in due course, instead of the standard guilty or not guilty verdict, they will have to consider whether he ‘committ The judge also told jurors that he would ‘strongly discourage’ them from setting up a group chat between themselves. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes The money is part of £10bn being handed out to regional mayors, councils, and housing associations across the country View 2 Images Tens of thousands of News Hannah Richardson 22:30, 24 Aug 2026 Updated 10:51, 25 Aug 2026 Andy Burnham is handing out £10 billion in a bid to ‘build the country out of a housing crisis’ as he says ‘no child should be raised in a hostel room’ Nationally, almost 180,000 children are growing up without a permanent home, the Government added. The allocations, which are wave one of Labour ’s £39bn 10-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme, aim to help families ‘trapped in temporary accommodation or stuck on housing wa The Prime Minister said the cash will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers to be spent on building ‘genuinely affordable homes’. Around 60pc of the more than 70,000 properties to be funded through the allocations are expected to be social rent Of the money up for grabs, Greater Manchester will be allocated £529 million – the largest share of any of the six mayoral areas that will benefit from this round. This is expected to deliver around 4,400 new homes, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said In November 2025, it was announced that Greater Manchester would ultimately benefit from £1.8bn from the Social and Affordable Homes Programme

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dovestones The Dovestone residents forced to take matters into their own hands as they are abused for driving home Nearly 1,000 fines were handed out last year but that has not stopped people ignoring the rules, according to those living near Doveston People living close to Dovestone Reservoir fear a ‘horrendous’ parking and traffic ‘nightmare’ could return now the area is back open to the public The area around the body of water, near Greenfield in Oldham , was closed for over a month following a devastating fire that destroyed a large area of moorland from July 11. People were ordered to stay away as emergency services and fire crews tackled the blaze The major incident was stood down on August 3 with crews at the scene for several days afterwards. On August 20, it was announced the roads and car park near the reservoir would reopen That has led to concerns among those living in the area, fearful of a major influx of visitors again, especially during periods of hot weather . More tourists has meant ‘local people tend to avoid it’ Before the fire, people said litter would pile up with ‘rubbish everywhere’, empty beer bottles would be left behind, and barbecues lit despite a ban. So many cars turn up, Sarah White said: “They were blocking the roads. You couldn’t even get through at the time.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester could soon become a 20mph city - but not everyone is convinced Hundreds more streets are set for lower speed limits, but some have questioned whether it is the right approach. Supposedly a 30mph area, the road cuts right across the estate from east to west but many locals say there’s a major speeding problem It has got to the point where some people ‘struggle to cross the road’ at certain times of day because of how fast the cars go, and the amount of traffic congestion But everything could soon change under plans by Manchester council to slash speed limits to 20mph on hundreds of roads around Wythenshawe, including Hollyhedge The move was announced in August to bring Wythenshawe’s roads in line with other parts of the city, and reduce collisions Speed limits in many parts of Manchester have fallen in recent years under the same aim, with nearly 70 per cent of the network now at 20mph according to council figures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Radcliffe Radcliffe man, 22, ends up in court after chat with cyclist left them 'backing away in fear' Tyreece Bedford appeared at Manchester Crown Court Comments News Hope Gallagher 06:00, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Tyreece Bedford A man swiped a man's hat after pulling out what police believe was a knife. Tyreece Bedford, 22, found himself in the dock following the 'tomfoolery' last summer Manchester Crown Court heard a man he knew cycled past him on Pilkington Way, Radcliffe , on June 14, 2025. The cyclist turned back and approached Bedford The pair briefly spoke before Bedford took the man's hat. When he tried to get it back, Bedford brandished an object cops believe was a blade CCTV footage played in court showed the man backing away from Bedford. He was initially charged with threatening a person with a blade and theft, but instead pleaded guilty to the lesser charge of affray Prosecutor Brian Berlyne said: "The man backed away in apparent fear. He appears to believe it to be a weapon. Police believe it to have been a small knife."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Armed police called to Cheshire village after shots fired A 35-year-old man has been arrested at the scene News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 21:43, 25 Aug 2026 Updated 21:53, 25 Aug 2026 View Image Beauty Bank, Cheshire A man has been arrested after gunshots were heard in a Cheshire village. Armed police were called to reports of the incident in the Beauty Bank area of Whitegate near Northwich at around 5.45pm on Monday (August 24) A 35-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm in a public place. An air weapon was also found during a search of the area Detective Inspector Ross Hamilton, of Northwich CID, said: “Firearms offences are rare in Cheshire, and we treat all reports we receive extremely seriously “While on this occasion there were no reports of any injuries, the use of firearms in a public place can be extremely dangerous and there are also a number of legal consequences, including significant custodial sentences “Enquiries in relation to this incident remain ongoing and I would urge anyone with any information or footage which may aid our enquiries to call us on 101 or visit www.cheshire.police.uk/tell-us quoting IML 2402957.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport for Greater Manchester New upgrades for train stations across Greater Manchester in £100m plan It includes improvements to make stations more accessible. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Market Look inside Bury Market’s much-anticipated new food hall The hall is expected to boast 12 food and retail units, a central bar and a stage News Hannah Richardson 18:38, 25 Aug 2026 View 3 Images CGI image of how Bury Market's new food hall New pictures and video show inside the much-anticipated new Bury Market food hall as work continues The new Casewells flexi-hall will be a place for people to eat, drink and watch performances, Bury council has said. It comes as a £33m investment into the world-famous market Work is continuing on site, but new footage and photos have been released by Bury council showing the progress of the two-floor, 22,000sq ft venue. When complete, the hall is expected to boast 12 food and retail units, a central bar and a stage View 3 Images Inside Bury Market's new food hall (Image: Bury council) The hall has been named after the first shop in Bury said to have sold black pudding. title: Stockport council announces big change to bin collections

evidence_packet.title: Stockport council announces big change to bin collections
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport w
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport w
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council announces big change to bin collections While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticism of Stockport council Comments News Edward Barne Thousands across Stockport will be affected by a major change to their bin collections later this year. The new system will be brought in before Christmas From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 The town hall’s Liberal Democrat administration said it has responded to complaints in recent weeks over how it collects bins across the borough. While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticis Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins. One resident called the situation ‘woke’, another said it was ‘petty’, and a councillor claimed some areas were being ‘pick More recently, the council was accused of flipflopping after a 'bizarre' incident was recorded on a doorbell camera, which the local authority later said was a mistake . Dave Bresnahan said: "It seems like they have gone from one extreme to another."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Sir Billy Boston: Wigan's greatest ever warrior A wad of cash spread out on a table in Cardiff led to an iconic rugby league career View 6 Images Sir Billy Boston News Paul Britton Reporter 16:29, 25 Aug 2026 A feared streak of pace combined with endless power and a ruthless desire to win Tough in the tackle - and even tougher to tackle as he graced the wings of rugby grounds across the world - Sir Billy Boston was arguably Wigan's greatest ever warrior. Yet outside of the sport his smile and personality were as endearing as his determination on the pitch was fier The rugby league legend, who has died aged 92 a month after the passing of his adored wife of 70 years, transcended generations He once scored more than 120 tries in one season alone and after being scouted by Wigan at the tender age of 19, he was the first non-white player to represent Great Britain during a Lions tour in 1954 - smashing a racial barrier in British sport His career as a globally-recognised, trailblazing black sports star inspired others to do what he was doing and work to achieve what he was achieving

title: The Mancunian Way: Stone the crows!

evidence_packet.title: The Mancunian Way: Stone the crows!
evidence_packet.lead: The wave one funding of Labour ’s £39bn ten-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers.
evidence_packet.summary: The wave one funding of Labour ’s £39bn ten-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers. Greater Manchester will be allocated £529 million – the largest share of any of the six mayoral areas that will b
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The wave one funding of Labour ’s £39bn ten-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers. Greater Manchester will be allocated £529 million – the largest share of any of the six mayoral areas that will b This is expected to deliver around 4,400 new homes with mayor Bev Craig claiming the region can “turn the tide” on the housing crisis with the right support from the Government. She has promised to build 50,000 new affordable homes across the region by 2039 View 7 Images ‌ Around 60 per cent of the more than 70,000 properties to be funded nationally through the allocations are expected to be for social rent But it’s not quite the plan that was originally pitched by Mr Burnham during his Makerfield by-election campaign. Back then he called for the entire £39 billion social and affordable homes programme to be spent on council housing And some have been quick to accuse the PM of watering down his ambitions. Housing minister Matthew Pennycook has rejected the suggestion “Andy Burnham said in the by-election that he wanted to see more money spent on social rent on council house building,” he told BBC Breakfast. “That’s exactly what we’re doing through this initial wave of funding.”

He is accused of offences of rape, intentional strangulation, supplying a class B drug (cannabis) and being concerned in the supply of a class A drug (crack coca The incident was reported to have happened near Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester city centre , at around 1.30am on July 14 At a plea hearing, Mr Shinwari entered not guilty pleas to all offences. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Trial of men accused of historic sexual offences against three girls in Rochdale due to start Tahir Rashid, Mohammed Saleem, Sucklane Shah, Amjad Mahmood, Iftaq Hussain and Arshad Mohammed deny all the charges they face News Andrew Bardsley Cou A jury in the trial of six men accused of historic sexual offences allegedly committed against three girls in Rochdale has been sworn in Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. Their trial at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester is due to begin tomorrow, (August 26) when jurors are set to hear the The complainants are referred to as Girl A, Girl B and Girl C for legal reasons. Jurors have heard that Mr Mahmood is unfit to stand trial and is not present in the dock Judge Matthew Corbett-Jones told the jury that he is ‘in hospital outside of the country receiving treatment for a complex psychiatric illness’. He told jurors that in due course, instead of the standard guilty or not guilty verdict, they will have to consider whether he ‘committ The judge also told jurors that he would ‘strongly discourage’ them from setting up a group chat between themselves. While he said some juries set up group chats to discuss logistic issues, he warned them that material discussing the case in such a group would be prohibited

evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An urgent plea for improved transport links for Leigh has been backed by members of Wigan Council It means Wigan Council will ask Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) and the new Mayor of Greater Manchester to consider ‘interim rapid transport systems’ while long term solutions – such as Metrolink – are assessed Councillor Cunliffe, told colleagues improvements are a “matter of urgency” for residents in and around Leigh, with higher frequency for existing services and smaller scale infrastructure projects required He said: “I know as being part of the Mayoral Development Zone things are happening to see about transport improvement and a feasibility study at getting Metrolink into Leigh. I welcome that “But big infrastructure projects can take years. There are things that can be done in the interim period and that is what we would like to explore.” He added that increased travel times into locations in Manchester city centre and surrounding areas leave residents socially excluded, causing “barriers to employment, education, and social mobility”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. Both have official sh Built in 2000 at the booming Salford Quays, this astonishing building is a shrine to all things art, with galleries, theatres, workshops, cafes and shops. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Chair and BID Director & Leasing Director at Orbit Developments Rhys, has been part of the Orbit team for over 20 years and has spent the last 15years working on a 400,000 square foot of Stockport town centre portfolio which includes offices, retail and business units Orbits involvement in the town centre started in the early 1970’s. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

evidence_packet.evidence_text: For almost a year, T Connect students have been joining us in the Manchester Digital office and getting a taste of what it really means to build a career in tech. It’s been a pleasure to have them with us. We’ve seen their curiosity, eagerness and passion for technology, as well But the success of T Connect has never been something Manchester Digital could deliver alone At its heart, T Connect is about building meaningful connections between technical education and the technology sector. That means giving students opportunities to meet people working in the industry, understand the different careers available to them and, crucially, put their sk Over the past year, businesses and individuals from across our community have helped make that possible in a huge variety of ways - from industry insight sessions and technical masterclasses to mentoring, work experience, office visits and live business projects Our students had the opportunity to learn directly from industry professionals, developing their technical knowledge and getting insight into the tools and approaches used in the workplace Hyperact - Jacob Clark, Director of Engineering, delivered a JavaScript masterclass, helping students strengthen their practical technical knowledge

title: What could greater devolution mean for Manchester's tech ecosystem? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: What could greater devolution mean for Manchester's tech ecosystem? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No
evidence_packet.summary: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No
evidence_packet.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. It should mean earlier engagement

title: From T Connect student to tech team member: how Hippo created a pathway into industry | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: From T Connect student to tech team member: how Hippo created a pathway into industry | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students wit
evidence_packet.summary: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students wit
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.lead: Murat Dalkılıç at Indigo at The O2
evidence_packet.summary: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки
evidence_packet.evidence_text: --> Murat Dalkılıç в Лондон ᐉ Билет на концерт Купить на 29 января 2027 ᐉ mticket.uk --> --> КОНЦЕРТЫ ТУРЫ ТЕАТР Добавить событие Условия использования Политика конфиденциальности Помощь --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> Личный кабинет Контакты --> --> 189279-136115 Афиша Великобритания » Лондон » КОНЦЕРТЫ » Indigo at The O2 » Murat Dalkılıç 47,70-90,10 GBP Купить билет #Поп #Поп-рок #Dance-Pop 29 января Murat Dalkılıç Лондон 47,70-90,10 GBP Лондон Indigo at The O2 205 Peninsula Square, London SE10 0ES, Great Britain Купить билет Поделиться в соцсетях Заказать билеты на "Murat Dalkılıç" Выбрать дату 29 янв. пятница --> --> --> 20:30 Открытие дверей: 19:00 47,70-90,10 GBP Купить билет О событии Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ

Drawing on real-world examples and lessons from delivery, the panel will explore what it takes to move from ambition and experimentation to measurable results The discussion will offer a candid view of the decisions, foundations and trade-offs involved. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
